answer.question: Does Arm A beat Arm R by >=1.5x on total uncached tokens?
answer.statement: YES: Arm A beats Arm R by 1.700x on total uncached tokens (51172 vs 30097). R and F are within 8.0% of each other, so the edit-vs-fork contrast is not the driver. Decomposition: only 1620 tokens of R's 20649-token excess over the control (7.8% of the gap) is net break cost at the two compaction turns; the other 19029 tokens (92.2%) is the post-compaction steady state, where R's short window re-prefills ~1660 tokens/turn against the control's ~755. The >=1.5x test passes, but the cost is window truncation-plus-break, not the break event alone: with the control's ambient residual and only the break effect, R would total 32143 and A/R would be 1.07x.

window_cost_of_never_compacting.note: Arm A never shrinks: every compaction appends a [note] node to the whole existing chain.  `extra_prompt_tokens_vs_control` is the token mass those notes add over the 40-turn window; `prompt_growth_tokens` is the window growth from first to last turn.

decomposition.note: R's total-uncached excess over the control splits into (a) the two scheduled break turns, measured net of C, and (b) the post-compaction steady state.  If (b) dominates, the arm-level ratio is a window/short-chain cost, not a break-event cost.
